title: Declarative Partitioning: Range, List, and Hash Strategies
realWorldScenario: The `events` table in SaaS analytics has reached 800 million rows (1.2 TB). Queries filtering by `created_at` are slow, and monthly data archiving requires deleting 70 million rows, which causes massive table bloat and lock contention.
questionStatement: Design a declarative table partitioning architecture for the `events` table by month using PostgreSQL 13+ declarative range partitioning. Explain partition pruning (run-time vs compile-time), local vs global index constraints, and how dropping a partition provides instant zero-bloat data retention.
expectedConcepts: PARTITION BY RANGE syntax and monthly child partitions
Partition key inclusion requirement in primary/unique keys
DROP TABLE / DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY for instant archiving
Lack of global indexes in PostgreSQL
hints: In PostgreSQL, why must the partition key be included in every UNIQUE constraint on the partitioned table?
Compare deleting 70 million rows via DELETE vs DROP TABLE.
Check DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY in PG 14+.
